newsitem.title: CHINA: Chirac China visit hastens Elf Atochem deals.
newsitem.headline: Chirac China visit hastens Elf Atochem deals.

text.p: This week's visit by French President Jacques Chirac to China has hastened the creation of a holding company and joint venture for Elf Atochem, the chemicals unit of Elf Aquitaine, the company said on Tuesday.
Chirac is scheduled to begin a four-day state visit to China on Thursday.

The visit had accelerated negotiations on a $20 million venture between Elf Atochem and China's Wuhan Organic Chemical Industry Co that would produce benzyl chloride and phenyl acetic acid, company chairman Jacques Puechal told a news conference.
"It has been speeded up by the visit of Chirac," Puechal said, adding that an agreement on the venture in central China's Wuhan city had been signed on May 6.
Chirac's arrival had also hastened approval for the creation of a China holding company for Elf Atochem, he said.
An agreement on the new company, which would have capital of $30 million and would provide services for the French firm's Chinese joint ventures, was signed on May 9.
"When we heard that Mr Chirac was planning to come here, we were very pleased... It's a very strong message in front of the world on how France and China can cooperate," Puechal said.
Elf Atochem's turnover in Greater China -- mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan -- was $200 million in 1996, and was expected to soar to $500 million by 2001, he said.
Mainland China accounted for about two-thirds of sales in the Greater China region, he said, but gave no details.
Imports accounted for around $150 million of the $200 million regional turnover last year, but by 2000 local production should account for two-thirds of sales, he said.

Almost all of the $300 million total investment earmarked by Elf Atochem for current projects in Greater China would go to the mainland, Puechal said. Further projects currently under consideration would require another $300 million.
